today.name: MOVO AI
today.tagline: The world's first long-form video agent for mobile
today.description: MOVO AI is the world’s first AI video agent for long-form creation that works right from your phone. It also works on the web. Shoot, upload, or start with an idea, then tell MOVO AI what you want. MOVO plans, creates, refines, keeps characters and scenes consistent, and brings the whole video together. Lock your phone and MOVO keeps working. Come back to review or make changes through chat. No prompt gymnastics. No canvas-heavy workflows. No manual clip stitching.

comments.text: Hi Product Hunt 👋I’m one of the makers behind MOVO AI—the world’s first long-form video agent on your mobile.My mother is a small creator who manages several social media accounts, and my father is her loyal cameraman. They are both over 60, but they still spend hours filming, editing, posting, and proudly watching every new like and follower.They make little, if any, money from it. But social media gives them something real: an audience, confidence, and the feeling that their stories are being seen.At the same time, I watched more founders around me become creators. They recorded videos between meetings, explained their ideas to customers, and built influence around themselves and their products.I was different. I was an introverted engineer who began working in AI while completing my graduate degree at Carnegie Mellon University. I had ideas, but I didn’t understand camera movements, editing, or how to look natural on camera. Even with the newest iPhone, I often didn’t know where to begin.My parents showed me how meaningful it could be to share your life. The founders around me showed me how necessary video was becoming. Together, they made me feel like I was being left behind by an era I was helping to build.That gap became the reason we built MOVO AI.What is MOVO?MOVO turns an idea into a complete long-form video through one continuous conversation.Start with a rough thought, script, reference, or a few assets. MOVO helps structure the story, establish the characters and visual direction, generate scenes, respond to feedback, and compose everything into a cohesive video.You don’t need to know the technical name of every shot or write a complex prompt for each scene. You can simply talk to MOVO as you would talk to a director, creative partner, or friend.Internally, we describe it as “Codex for video”: you direct what you want to create without writing every underlying instruction yourself.What surprised usWe initially thought eliminating prompt gymnastics would mainly help beginners. Professional AI creators already knew how to write sophisticated prompts, select models, and manage complicated workflows.We underestimated how much professionals would value this approach too.They embraced it not because they couldn’t write prompts, but because they wanted to focus their attention on what matters more: story, structure, pacing, characters, and emotion.Conversations with accomplished professors and screenwriters at USC’s School of Cinematic Arts reinforced this belief. Models and production tools will keep changing, but storytelling remains the foundation.We realized that agentic creation is not simply an easier mode for beginners. It may be a more universal creative interface: accessible enough for a first-time creator, yet powerful enough to free professionals from repetitive production work.Why mobile mattersOnce creation becomes conversational, it no longer needs to live inside a desktop canvas.A founder can start a product video before the next meeting. A store owner can review an advertisement from behind the counter. A parent can develop a family story in the park. A filmmaker can approve scenes while moving between locations. A hiker can capture an idea at the summit before the inspiration disappears.You might describe an idea over breakfast, approve the storyboard on the train, review generated scenes after work, and refine the ending before bed.MOVO continues working asynchronously, so you don’t need to babysit every generation. Creation can move with your life instead of requiring your life to stop.From one video to an ongoing worldWithin the same project, you can begin Episodes 2, 3, and 4 in new sessions without re-entering the same characters, products, locations, and creative direction.MOVO carries that context forward, helping you develop an ongoing world rather than a collection of disconnected clips.What we’d love you to testWe would especially value feedback on three things:Does talking to MOVO feel like working with a useful director or creative partner?Can you meaningfully develop a video on mobile without supervising every step?How well does MOVO preserve your creative world across multiple episodes?AI video still has many unsolved problems, and MOVO is still evolving. We want to hear where it understands your direction, where it surprises you, and where it falls short.Our goal is not to replace human creativity. It is to close the gap between having a story and being able to show it.Anyone with a story should be able to make it move—wherever life takes them.Your idea. Moved by MOVO. 🎬

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt 👋 Back in April we launched Ovren here — you describe a coding task in plain words, and it comes back as a pull request your team reviews. Thank you for the #4 of the day. The most common thing we heard after that launch: "I trust the pull request… but I can't read code. How do I know it's what I asked for?" So today we're launching Live Preview. Here's how it works: 1. Connect your GitHub project (one GitHub App install) 2. Describe the change — "add a testimonials section under the hero, matching our card style" 3. Ovren plans it, you approve the plan, it writes the code on a safe copy of your project 4. You get a live preview — your real page, with the change on it. Click through it like a visitor would 5. Happy? Approve it, and your developers review and merge the pull request. Not happy? Request changes. No localhost, no install, no deploy. Ovren builds the preview on its side. What it's for: → Marketers and founders who want to see a landing section, banner or form before asking anyone to merge it → PMs who want to show stakeholders a working version, not a mockup → Developers who'd rather click through a change than read a diff of someone else's request To be upfront: live preview covers frontend changes. Backend work still comes as a pull request with a full execution report — what Ovren understood, the files it changed and any risks it flagged. You can try it free — up to 5 changes, no credit card. I'd love to hear what you'd ship first, and what would make you trust a preview enough to approve it. I'm here all day 🙌

today.name: Cloudflare Clairic

today.description: Clairic is Cloudflare's new AI model for extracting structured information without generating tokens. Give it messy text or images, and it returns typed values like names, dates, amounts, calculations, and estimates in a single pass, with confidence scores. Built for developers who need faster, cheaper data processing than traditional LLM calls. Available in preview on Workers AI at $0.10 per million input tokens, with open weights planned.

comments.text: Cloudflare just released Clairic, and I think the idea behind it is pretty interesting. We're using LLMs for all sorts of tasks that don't really need text generation — extracting invoice totals, reading dates, pulling information from documents, etc. Clairic is built specifically for that kind of work. It returns structured values in a single pass, without generating tokens one by one. It's also just $0.10 per million input tokens on Workers AI. Still an early preview, but I'm curious to see how these smaller, specialized models change the way we build AI applications.

Hi Product Hunt,I'm Arick, co-founder and CEO of BAND. Today we're launching BAND for Developers.If you run more than one coding agent, you know the pattern. Each agent is fast on its own, but they can't talk to each other, so you become the go-between. You copy context from one session into the next, tell the test agent what the refactor agent just changed, and find out an hour later that two agents made opposite assumptions about the same interface. More agents should mean more work done. Instead, a lot of it turns into more coordination for you.Most multi-agent dev tools today give you a better dispatch board. You assign tasks, agents run in parallel, you review what comes back. That helps with throughput, but every handoff still goes through a human.BAND for Developers lets the agents work it out between themselves:- Connect the agents you already run. Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot and OpenCode agents join shared rooms across machines. You keep your IDE, your terminal and your workflow.- Agents collaborate directly. They message each other, delegate, review each other's work and unblock one another. They can pull in a teammate's agent when the work needs it. Plans, decisions and work state live in the room rather than inside one session, so they survive when a session ends.- You step in when it matters. You keep working from the terminal. Full disclosure — I'm a big fan of Anthropic and actually built an app that works exclusively with Claude Desktop for secure local file search. So I've spent a lot of time thinking about this space.My concern with Cowork isn't the vision, it's the architecture. Agentic tasks burn through tokens fast (Anthropic says so themselves), so that $200/month cap can disappear quicker than you'd expect. And at that price, you'd want to use it for real work — but the whole thing requires giving Claude direct read/write/delete access to your files. If you're handling client data, patient records, or anything regulated, you're basically out.The bigger issue is prompt injection. Anthropic admits "the chances of an attack are still non-zero" — and back in October 2025, researchers showed exactly that: a prompt injection against Claude that pulled up to 30MB of user data per request through Anthropic's own API. When you're talking about an agent with file system access, email connectors, and a browser, that's not some theoretical edge case.There's a reason some of us build tools where Claude can search your files without actually touching them. The agentic future is definitely coming, but "AI that can access everything" and "AI that keeps you in control" are two very different products for two very different users.

year.name: Upstream
year.tagline: The inbox designed for humans and agents
year.description: Finally, an inbox you'll look forward to. Agents sort your messages, draft your replies, and clear the grunt work behind the scenes, all in a client so well-crafted that email feels light, fast, fun.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt! 👋 Louis here, co-founder of Upstream.When I was at Algolia, I was drowning in 200 emails a day. I was never sure where to focus, and getting through my inbox took forever. I knew it didn’t have to be this way. Instead of creating a new messaging protocol, I bet on rethinking the tool everyone uses: email.We built the first email client where agents do real work alongside people. We designed Upstream to be easy to pick up and fun to use. 📥 Take the noise out of emailAgents automatically triage your inbox, separate signal from noise, and surface only what deserves your attention✍️ Every reply starts with a draftUpstream drafts replies for every conversation that needs one. It also changes your voice based on who you’re talking to and the context of the convo⏰ Never miss a follow-upAgents track open loops and remind you when needed, making sure important conversations don't fall through the cracks🔎 Ask anything about your workAI can instantly find information across your inbox and connected tools: receipts, meeting notes, introductions, decisions, conversations, and more🔗 Bring all your context into your inboxAgents use information from tools like Notion, Calendar, Drive, Granola, and other sources to produce better answers and drafts👉 As a special thank you to the Product Hunt community, you get one free month of Upstream Pro if you sign up at upstream.do and use the code PH26! 👈We are all so excited to hear what you think!
